question:
Let $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be defined by $f(x)=x^3$.

(i) Show that $f$ is one-one.

(ii) Determine whether $f$ is onto and justify your answer.
explanation:
(i) Verification of the one-one property
Let $x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{Z}$ and suppose $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$. Then
$$x_1^3=x_2^3.$$
This implies
$$x_1=x_2.$$
Hence, $f$ is one-one.

(ii) Testing the onto property
Consider $2\in\mathbb{Z}$. For $2$ to have a pre-image, there must exist $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
$$x^3=2.$$
No integer satisfies this equation. Therefore, $2$ has no pre-image in $\mathbb{Z}$.

Conclusion
The function $f$ is one-one but not onto.

options.D: $f$ is one-one but not onto because integers such as $2$ have no integer pre-image
